output.summary: The district hires Spartan Medical, Inc. to provide site coordinators or medical staff to help run its COVID-19 testing program, for up to $3,672,000 from October 13, 2021 through October 12, 2022. The board is using a sole source exception, which lets the district skip public bidding when it finds only one provider can do the work.

output.headline: Approves Measure G1 grant and spending plan for United for Success Academy for 2021-22
output.summary: The board adopts a resolution recommended by the Measure G1 (teacher retention and middle school improvement) oversight commission. It approves a 2021-2022 grant application and education spending plan for United for Success Academy (grades 6-8), using the school's approved 2021-2022 funding allocation. The item does not state a dollar amount.

output.headline: Ratifies free use of International Community School space by California Children's Services
output.summary: The board ratifies (approves after the fact) an agreement letting Alameda County California Children Services use designated spaces at International Community School. The agency provides occupational therapy and physical therapy to students, at no cost to the district.

output.headline: Approves up to $165,000 for AssetWorks to verify the district's equipment inventory in 2022

money.evidence: not to exceed $165,000.00

output.summary: AssetWorks of Pittsburgh will visit district sites and verify the inventory of machinery and equipment that cost $500 or more, covering all additions, disposals and transfers since the last physical inventory as of June 30, 2019. The work helps the district meet financial reporting rules and its own inventory policies. It runs January 10 to December 31, 2022, for no more than $165,000.

output.headline: Proclaims October 2021 as Principals' Month to honor the district's school leaders
output.summary: This resolution names October 2021 as the district's Principals' Month in honor of all of its school leaders. The agenda text lists no dollar amounts.

output.headline: Accepts $531,958 from First 5 of Alameda County for Summer Pre-K and school readiness work

money.evidence: in the amount of $531,958.00

output.summary: The district accepts a $531,958 grant from First 5 of Alameda County. The money supports Summer Pre-K programs, training for early childhood and K-12 teachers, a School Readiness Coordinator, and financial relief for families with children ages 0-5 in the highest-need Oakland neighborhoods. It covers July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022.
